# Comparable [weather data]{.accent}, from any [source]{.accent}

::: lead-text
mlwp-tools is a small set of Python packages that turn forecasts, observations and reanalyses into `xarray` datasets you can safely compare: a shared contract, your own loader, and alignment that works out *how* to align from *what* each dataset is.
:::
:::

::: hero-actions
[Get started <i class="bi bi-arrow-right"></i>](get-started.qmd){.btn-cta}
[<i class="bi bi-github"></i> GitHub](https://github.com/mlwp-tools){.btn-ghost}
:::
::::

:::: {}
::: terminal
::: terminal-bar
forecast_vs_synop.py
:::

```python
import mlwp_data_loaders as dl
import mxalign as mx
import scores

# load + validate: tag with traits, check against the specs
ds_obs = dl.load_and_validate_dataset(
    "obs.sqlite",
    loader="mlwp_data_loaders.loaders.harp.obstable",
)
ds_fc = dl.load_and_validate_dataset(
    "fc.nc",
    loader="mlwp_data_loaders.loaders.anemoi.anemoi_inference",
)

# align: grid -> stations, then common valid times
ds_fc_aligned = mx.align_space(ds_fc, reference=ds_obs)
ds_obs_aligned, ds_fc_aligned = mx.align_time(
    [ds_obs, ds_fc_aligned]
)

# score: any metrics package works, or your own function
da_rmse = scores.continuous.rmse(
    ds_fc_aligned["2t"],
    ds_obs_aligned["2t"],
    preserve_dims=["lead_time"],
)
```
:::

## Every source speaks its own format

::: lead-text
Verifying a forecast means putting it next to something else: observations, an analysis, another model. Each of those arrives in its own format, with its own dimension names, coordinates, units and conventions.
:::

::: {.card-grid .card-grid-5}

::: mt-card
::: card-icon
<i class="bi bi-cloud-sun"></i>
:::
### Forecasts
GRIB, netCDF, Zarr, FA, ML model output from anemoi-inference and friends.
:::

::: mt-card
::: card-icon
<i class="bi bi-geo-alt"></i>
:::
### Observations
BUFR, HARP SQLite obstables, `vobs` files, station networks.
:::

::: mt-card
::: card-icon
<i class="bi bi-box-seam"></i>
:::
### Reanalysis
Zarr and netCDF archives such as ERA5 and regional reanalyses.
:::

::: mt-card
::: card-icon
<i class="bi bi-globe2"></i>
:::
### Satellite
BUFR, SEVIRI native and HRIT, HDF-EOS, …
:::

::: mt-card
::: card-icon
<i class="bi bi-broadcast"></i>
:::
### Radar
ODIM HDF5 composites and national radar products.
:::

:::

::: pull-quote
Before you can compare anything, you have to **align** it. That step gets rewritten, ad hoc, in every verification study. mlwp-tools is about writing it once.
:::

The idea
:::

## Bring your own loader

::: lead-text
One approach is a single general reader that understands every format. mlwp-tools makes the opposite bet: agree on a **minimal contract** for how a dataset should look, and let whoever knows the data best write the loader. That is usually around fifteen lines of `xarray`.
:::

Once a dataset follows the contract, a machine can answer the questions that a plain `xr.open_dataset` leaves open. Is this a forecast or an observation? A grid or scattered points? Deterministic, an ensemble, or quantiles? Every dataset declares three **traits**, and everything else follows from them.
::::

:::: {}
::: traits-table

| Trait | Attribute | Values |
|---|---|---|
| **Space** | `mlwp_space_trait` | `grid` · `point` |
| **Time** | `mlwp_time_trait` | `forecast` · `observation` · `climatology` |
| **Uncertainty** | `mlwp_uncertainty_trait` | `deterministic` · `ensemble` · `quantile` |

:::

Each trait implies the dimensions, coordinates and metadata (`standard_name`, `units`) a dataset must have. That is all a loader has to satisfy, nothing more.
::::

## Contract → load → align

::: lead-text
Three packages, each with one job. They share one data model: **everything is an `xr.Dataset`**. The specs validate it, loaders tag it, mxalign aligns it. There is no new data structure to learn.
:::

::: {.card-grid .card-grid-3}

::: mt-card
::: layer-num
01 · Contract
:::
### mlwp-data-specs
Defines the three traits and validates any `xr.Dataset` or Zarr store against them, from Python, the command line or CI. The spec text and the checks live side by side.
:::

::: mt-card
::: layer-num
02 · Load
:::
### mlwp-data-loaders
Turns raw files into datasets that pass the specs. Built-in loaders for anemoi-inference, anemoi-datasets, HARP obstables and IFS forecasts, or point it at your own function.
:::

::: mt-card
::: layer-num
03 · Align
:::
### mxalign
Reads the traits and picks the right alignment: grid to points, forecasts to observations, onto common valid times. Lazy with Dask, from a notebook up to a Slurm cluster.
:::

:::

::: flow-wrap
```{mermaid}
%%| fig-responsive: true
flowchart LR
  S1[(Anemoi<br/>inference)] --> L1[built-in loader]
  S2[(HARP<br/>obstable)] --> L2[built-in loader]
  S3[(your own<br/>format)] --> L3[your loader]
  L1 --> U[[xr.Dataset]]
  L2 --> U
  L3 --> U
  U --> V{{validate traits<br/>mlwp-data-specs}}
  V --> X[[spec-conforming<br/>xr.Dataset]]
  X --> A[align in space & time<br/>mxalign]
  A --> M[metrics, scorecards,<br/>HARP verification]
```
:::

## The toolbox

::: lead-text
All packages are open source and developed on GitHub under the [mlwp-tools](https://github.com/mlwp-tools) organisation. Releases are tag-driven and published to PyPI; see the [roadmap](roadmap.md) for what is coming next.
:::

::: {.card-grid .card-grid-3}

::: mt-card
[v0.1.0 on PyPI]{.badge-status .badge-released}

### [mlwp-data-specs]{.pkg-name}
Trait specifications and a validator for MLWP datasets, with a CLI and a Python API.

::: card-links
[GitHub](https://github.com/mlwp-tools/mlwp-data-specs) [Spec docs](https://mlwp-tools.github.io/mlwp-data-specs/) [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/mlwp-data-specs/)
:::
:::

::: mt-card
[First release soon]{.badge-status}

### [mlwp-data-loaders]{.pkg-name}
Loaders that create spec-conforming `xr.Dataset`s from anemoi, HARP and IFS data, or from your own code.

::: card-links
[GitHub](https://github.com/mlwp-tools/mlwp-data-loaders)
:::
:::

::: mt-card
[v0.1.0 on PyPI · v0.2 soon]{.badge-status .badge-released}

### [mxalign]{.pkg-name}
Space and time alignment of meteorological datasets, plus a config-driven pipeline on Dask.

::: card-links
[GitHub](https://github.com/mlwp-tools/mxalign) [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/mxalign/)
:::
:::

::: mt-card
[In development]{.badge-status}

### [mlwp-harp-writer]{.pkg-name}
Writes aligned datasets to HARP parquet, so harp's point verification tools can read them directly.

::: card-links
[GitHub](https://github.com/mlwp-tools/mlwp-harp-writer)
:::
:::

::: mt-card
[In development]{.badge-status}

### [mlwp-scorecard]{.pkg-name}
Scorecards that show at a glance where a forecast system beats a baseline, and where it is worse.

::: card-links
[GitHub](https://github.com/mlwp-tools/mlwp-scorecard)
:::
:::

## We hand you arrays that are safe to compare

::: lead-text
Plenty of packages already compute metrics well. Once your datasets share the same space, time and units, a score is a one-liner: bring `xskillscore`, `scores` or your own function.
:::

When one notebook is not enough, mxalign runs the same steps from a YAML config (load, transform, align, score) over Dask, on your laptop or on a Slurm cluster. The metric is configuration, not code we own.

::: hero-actions
[Walk through an example <i class="bi bi-arrow-right"></i>](get-started.qmd){.btn-ghost}
:::
::::

:::: {}
::: terminal
::: terminal-bar
config.yaml
:::

```yaml
datasets:
  ai-lam:
    loader: mlwp_data_loaders.loaders.anemoi.anemoi_inference
    files: ai-lam/{reference_time:strftime(%Y%m%d%H)}.nc
  synop:
    loader: mlwp_data_loaders.loaders.harp.obstable
    files: OBSTABLE.sqlite
alignment:
  reference: synop
  space:
    interpolation:
      method: delaunay
verification:
  reference: synop
  metrics:
    rmse:
      function: xskillscore.rmse  # any callable
      dim: ["reference_time", "point_index"]
```
:::

## Get involved

::: lead-text
mlwp-tools started as a collaboration between people at European weather services working on machine-learning weather prediction, and it is open to anyone who needs to compare weather datasets. New loaders, bug reports and ideas for the specs are all welcome.
:::

- **Code and issues**: [github.com/mlwp-tools](https://github.com/mlwp-tools). Open an issue or a pull request on any of the packages.
- **Where things are heading**: the [roadmap](roadmap.md) lists the planned releases and the open decisions.
- **Talk to us**: we meet ad hoc; get in touch through a GitHub issue to join.
::::

:::: {}
::: mt-card
::: card-icon
<i class="bi bi-people"></i>
:::
### Ways to contribute

- **Add a loader** for a data source you work with.
- **Report** a dataset that doesn't validate, or a spec that is unclear.
- **Discuss** the trait specs and what they should cover next.

::: card-links
[Open an issue <i class="bi bi-arrow-right"></i>](https://github.com/mlwp-tools)
